statusDetail: The requested host redirected to https://xhamster46.desi/. Five representative paths were judged with all 58 catalog checks recorded. Excluded: authenticated account management, payment completion, actual identity verification and creator upload, because they require credentials, identity documents or commercial commitment; their entry/disclosure states were reviewed where reachable.

page.framework: Vue-like server-rendered application (framework markers in rendered HTML)
page.notes: Public media/listing site with strong server-rendered content, client hydration, service worker and domain redirect from xhamster45.desi to xhamster46.desi.

paths.description: Homepage and video listing template; represents discovery, navigation, consent, preferences, performance and network behaviour.
Category index template; represents taxonomy navigation and dense listing UI.
Representative video detail and primary viewing journey, including the legal age-verification gate.
Account creation journey, including OAuth and email form disclosure/autofill behaviour.
Unknown-route recovery state; represents HTTP/navigation failure handling.

findings.summary: The interface is hard-coded dark rather than adapting to the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark emulation screenshots retain the same dark surfaces, while the computed root color-scheme is "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces/text through theme tokens or light-dark() so system preference controls the initial theme.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found eight running animations, each with a 2000 ms duration, while prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential looping animation and use immediate or minimal-opacity state changes.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM feature inspection found no view-transition usage across a navigation-heavy site.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document transitions for menu/filter state and cross-document transitions for compatible route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The large multi-row header and promotional chrome do not adapt as the long feed scrolls.
findings.evidence: The homepage screenshot shows three persistent header/banner rows; feature inspection found no scroll-state or animation-timeline implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query to compact sticky navigation after scrolling while preserving the current section and controls.

findings.summary: Navigation menus are custom dropdowns without native popover or anchor-positioning primitives.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains dropdown CSS chunks but zero popover elements and no anchor-positioning markers.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover with CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and tooltips, retaining a fallback for older browsers.

findings.summary: A large cookie consent panel obscures the primary listing on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and category screenshots show the consent panel centered over core content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep Reject as prominent as Accept, but move non-essential detail into a compact, semantic consent surface that does not cover the main task and restores focus correctly.

findings.summary: Modal experiences use role=dialog on generic containers instead of the dialog element.
findings.evidence: The signup DOM uses a div with role="dialog" and aria-modal="true"; the homepage feature probe found zero dialog and popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal account flows and popover for transient UI, relying on showModal(), close, focus management and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Navigation, age verification, sale promotion, side navigation and consent compete with the first content viewport.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot devotes most of the first viewport to three header rows, a left rail and a consent overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation into a drawer, remove or defer non-essential promotion, and reserve the first viewport for the primary listing.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into a 360 px viewport and requires horizontal panning.
findings.evidence: The narrow layout primitive measured scrollWidth 1024 px against a 360 px visual viewport, with 664 px overflow; the screenshot shows clipped navigation and cards. Signup has the same 664 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an intrinsic single-column mobile layout, fluid sizes, wrapping navigation and responsive card grids; ensure layout width never exceeds the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The 360 px capture preserves the desktop side rail and card widths; DOM feature inspection found no @container usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare container-type on reusable listing regions and use @container rules to switch card density, metadata and controls based on available space.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too short for comfortable touch use.
findings.evidence: The input probe found many links only 20 px high; Lighthouse target-size failed. Programmatic focus did retain a visible 3 px outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24 by 24 CSS px targets with spacing, preferably 44 px for primary touch controls, while retaining the visible focus indicator.

findings.summary: Mobile Largest Contentful Paint misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.9 s and FCP at 2.4 s. The separate desktop trace was faster at 1.22 s LCP, showing the mobile condition is the risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the mobile LCP element, prioritize only that resource, reduce initial server/document latency and defer work not needed for the first viewport.

findings.summary: The initial route has multiple render-blocking stylesheet candidates and a broad dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 147 requests and identified three VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheet candidates; DOM confirmation shows they are head stylesheets. Scripts are mostly correctly deferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline minimal critical CSS, split route styles, preload only the actual LCP asset and defer non-critical component CSS.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates the transferred page weight.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 62 scripts transferring 1,003,358 bytes; the largest route bundle alone transferred 401,971 bytes and Google sign-in added 98,505 bytes before signup intent.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure route coverage, split the index bundle, lazy-load authentication and secondary locale/features on intent, and remove duplicated or unused code.

findings.summary: Interactive controls have missing or mismatched accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name and label-content-name-mismatch; the DOM probe independently found an icon-only button and category filter input without labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon control an aria-label, associate persistent labels with inputs and ensure visible control text is included in the accessible name.

findings.summary: Important text fails WCAG contrast requirements in the normal theme.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.15:1 and 1.75:1 text on the green age banner and 3.29:1 secondary metadata on dark surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/background contrast to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and test semantic color tokens in all states.

findings.summary: Many images lack intrinsic dimensions and several are oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 29 of 36 images without width/height and 14 oversized relative to rendered width; eight below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every thumbnail, request a source close to rendered size, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: The detail page lacks structured VideoObject metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found a descriptive title, description and h1 but zero JSON-LD blocks on a rich video entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD matching visible title, thumbnail, duration, upload date, content URL and access restrictions, plus complete Open Graph preview tags.

findings.summary: Cookie and browser-policy hardening is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Three of four cookies lacked Secure; two used SameSite=None. CSP only declares frame-ancestors, HSTS is one day, and X-Content-Type-Options plus an HTTP Referrer-Policy header are absent; the page meta explicitly uses unsafe-url referrer policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use the narrowest SameSite/HttpOnly settings, deploy a full nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, a longer HSTS policy and strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: Third-party requests dominate the initial page before explicit feature intent.
findings.evidence: HAR counted 118 third-party requests transferring 1.57 MB of 1.68 MB total, across 12 third-party origins, including Google account code and an advertising syndicate.
findings.suggestedFix: Classify vendors, proxy or self-host essential static assets, delay Google identity and ads until relevant consent/intent, batch analytics and enforce a vendor budget.

findings.summary: Account creation offers OAuth or password but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The signup flow exposes Google, X and email/password options; no WebAuthn/passkey affordance or credential API use was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside existing recovery options, and request credentials only after explicit user intent.

findings.summary: The email signup path disables email autofill and relies on placeholder-only labelling.
findings.evidence: After expanding email signup, both email inputs reported autocomplete="off"; one had no placeholder or aria-label, while the password correctly used new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a labelled type=email field with autocomplete="email" and keep autocomplete="new-password" on the password field.

taskList.title: Rebuild narrow-screen layout and component reflow
Fix accessible names, contrast, zoom and target sizing
Harden cookies, CSP and privacy/security response policy
Replace intrusive/custom overlays with semantic content-first primitives
Improve mobile LCP and image delivery
Add passkeys and correct signup autofill
Adopt modern navigation transitions and positioning
